What it means: The City Council Committee on Ways and Means met virtually on October 6, 2026 [08:02, 08:26]. The hearing considered ten dockets [09:57] to transfer approximately $517,000 [09:46, 19:51] from the collective bargaining reserve [09:49] to cover fiscal year 2027 contract raises [09:55] for Boston Public Schools employee groups [09:28]. These groups include school police patrolmen, school police superior officers, planning and engineering staff, plant administrators, and storekeepers [09:32, 09:41]. The proposed agreements generally offer a 2 percent base wage increase along with flat dollar salary additions [11:10, 11:18, 12:35, 14:04, 15:13, 16:34].

Who moved it: Mayor Michelle Wu sponsored the dockets [16:47], which were referred to the committee on September 30, 2026 [16:50]. Committee Chair Weber [08:01, 18:25] hosted the hearing with Councilors Murphy, Flynn, Louijeune, Fitzgerald, Culpepper, and Worrell attending [17:09, 17:13, 21:27, 21:41]. A panel consisting of City Budget Director John Williamson, BPS Labor Relations Director Jeremiah, BPS Safety Services Chief Executive Director Izzy Marrero, and BPS Chief Operating Officer Brian Ford represented the administration [17:20, 17:25, 17:39, 17:42, 18:29].

What to watch: The chair indicated that the council intends to vote on the orders at its next meeting [18:56, 50:09]. Councilor Flynn asked to receive a copy of an unsigned memorandum of understanding between BPS and the Boston Police Department before the vote [43:24, 45:02, 46:04]. Members and public testifiers also raised questions about BPS staffing [37:34, 38:58, 40:48] and a state Inspector General report [24:20, 47:04, 48:16], but the transcript does not record any formal vote taking place during the hearing [50:09, 50:35].

summary: On October 6, 2026, the Boston City Council Committee on Ways and Means held a hearing to review proposed collective bargaining agreements and supplemental funding appropriations, including Dockets 1829, 1832, 1833, 1834, and 1837, for Boston Public Schools union personnel [08:02] [09:25] [10:09]. Budget officials described contract terms covering wage increases and transfers from the collective bargaining reserve to department budgets for school police, plant administrators, planning professionals, storekeepers, and delivery workers through fiscal year 2027 [09:55] [19:24] [20:29]. Councilors questioned panelists about public safety staffing vacancies [37:26] [39:37], the status of paraprofessional positions [40:44], the impact of a recent Inspector General report regarding procurement and mismanagement [24:22] [28:10], and requested a copy of an unsigned Memorandum of Understanding between the Boston Police Department and Boston Public Schools [44:01] [46:06]. Public testimony raised further concerns about long-term financial impacts and district oversight reforms [47:28] [48:19]. No votes were taken during the meeting, and the chair concluded the hearing to prepare the dockets for a full council vote [50:09] [50:36].
